arxiv-1704-06032.title: Space-charge effect of the time-varying electron injection in a diode: classical and relativistic regimes Drafted November 2016, revised 18 April 2017, POP51880 submitted 20 April, review received 1 May, revised 28 June and 16 July, POP51880A resubmitted 16 July, minor rev received 26 July, POP51880
arxiv-1704-06032.creator: Yangjié Liu (刘泱杰), Qi Tang, Biyi Wu (吴比翼)
arxiv-1704-06032.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Yangjié Liu (刘泱杰), Qi Tang, Biyi Wu (吴比翼). Conventionally, space-charge (SC) limited current density is defined as the maximal current density allowed to traverse a diode under a DC voltage when a time-invariant flow is injected from the cathode. In this work, we study the SC limited current density under a time-varying injection for both classical and relativistic regimes and determine the maximal amount of limited current density under certain conditions.

arxiv-2301-04261.title: Towards Microstructural State Variables in Materials Systems
arxiv-2301-04261.creator: Veera Sundararaghavan, Megna Shah and Jeff Simmons
arxiv-2301-04261.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Veera Sundararaghavan, Megna Shah and Jeff Simmons. The vast combination of material properties seen in nature are achieved by the complexity of the material microstructure. Advanced characterization and physics based simulation techniques have led to generation of extremely large microstructural datasets. There is a need for machine learning techniques that can manage data complexity by capturing the maximal amount of information about the microstructure using the least number of variables.

arxiv-2309-07053.title: Pearl’s and Jeffrey’s Update as Modes of Learning in Probabilistic Programming Journal: Electronic Notes in Theoretical Informatics and Computer Science Volume: 3
arxiv-2309-07053.creator: Bart Jacobs & Dario Stein
arxiv-2309-07053.description: Abstract The concept of updating a probability distribution in the light of new evidence lies at the heart of statistics and machine learning. Pearl’s and Jeffrey’s rule are two natural update mechanisms which lead to different outcomes, yet the similarities and differences remain mysterious.

arxiv-2312-08492.title: A Multi-Harmonic NIR-UV Dual-Comb Spectrometer
arxiv-2312-08492.creator: Kristina F. Chang, Daniel M. B. Lesko, Carter Mashburn, Peter Chang, Eugene Tsao, Alexander J. Lind, Scott A. Diddams
arxiv-2312-08492.description: Abstract Dual-comb spectroscopy in the ultraviolet (UV) and visible would enable broad bandwidth electronic spectroscopy with unprecedented frequency resolution. However, there are significant challenges in generation, detection and processing of dual-comb data that have restricted its progress in this spectral region. In this work, we leverage robust 1550 nm few-cycle pulses to generate frequency combs in the UV-visible.

arxiv-2503-07509.title: Interference-Aware Super-Constellation Design for NOMA Thanks: This work was supported by the by the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) under Grant ECCS-2301778.
arxiv-2503-07509.creator: Mojtaba Vaezi † and Xinliang Zhang ‡
arxiv-2503-07509.description: Abstract Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has gained significant attention as a potential next-generation multiple access technique. However, its implementation with finite-alphabet inputs faces challenges. Particularly, due to inter-user interference, superimposed constellations may have overlapping symbols leading to high bit error rates when successive interference cancellation (SIC) is applied. To tackle the issue, this paper employs autoencoders to design interference-aware super-constellations.

arxiv-2503-10084.title: Why Prompt Design Matters and Works: A Complexity Analysis of Prompt Search Space in LLMs
arxiv-2503-10084.creator: Xiang Zhang, Juntai Cao, Jiaqi Wei, Chenyu You, Dujian Ding
arxiv-2503-10084.description: Abstract Despite the remarkable successes of Large Language Models (LLMs), the underlying Transformer architecture has inherent limitations in handling complex reasoning tasks. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has emerged as a practical workaround, but most CoT-based methods rely on a single generic prompt like “think step by step,” with no task-specific adaptation.

arxiv-2508-10818.title: Controlling complex rhythms: A hierarchical approach to limit cycle switching
arxiv-2508-10818.creator: Sandip Saha, Suvam Pal, Dibakar Ghosh
arxiv-2508-10818.description: Abstract Limit cycles are self-sustained, closed trajectories in phase space representing (un)-stable, periodic behavior in nonlinear dynamical systems. They underpin diverse natural phenomena, from neuronal firing patterns to engineering oscillations. The presence of multiple concentric limit cycles reflects distinct behavioral symmetries within a system.

pmc-11534903.title: Branched-chain amino acids and their metabolites decrease human and rat hepatic stellate cell activation
pmc-11534903.creator: Maria Camila Trillos-Almanza, Magnolia Martinez Aguilar, Manon Buist-Homan, Nils Bomer, Karla Arevalo Gomez, Vincent E de Meijer, Frederike G I van Vilsteren, Hans Blokzijl, Han Moshage
pmc-11534903.description: BackgroundEnd-stage liver diseases (ESLDs) are a significant global health challenge due to their high prevalence and severe health impacts. Despite the severe outcomes associated with ESLDs, therapeutic options remain limited. Targeting the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), key drivers of extracellular matrix accumulation during liver injury presents a novel therapeutic approach.

pmc-12429376.title: Mix Design and Early-Age Performance of Rapid-Setting Phosphate-Based CBPCs for Emergency Road Repair
pmc-12429376.creator: Jaeyoung Lee
pmc-12429376.description: This study investigates rapid-setting, phosphate-based, chemically bonded phosphate ceramic (CBPC) composites for emergency pothole repair through a two-phase experimental approach. Phase I involved fundamental mix design experiments that systematically examined the effects of water-to-binder ratio (20–40%), filler content (10–50%), and phosphate powder fineness (570–3640 cm2/g) on setting and mechanical performance.

Malaria remains one of the most significant public health challenges in Uganda, particularly among children under 5 years of age.

pmc-12580446.description: Background and AimsHospital nutrition is an essential component of the multidisciplinary care of COVID‐19 patients. Malnourished COVID‐19 patients present more symptoms, complications, and require longer hospitalization times. Therefore, the aim of the present investigation was to study the influence of an advanced and careful hospital nutrition on COVID‐19 patients' evolution and treatment.

pmc-13256005.title: Urgent investment needed to reclaim lactation care and training to support Indigenous women, babies, families, and communities
pmc-13256005.creator: Georgia Stewart, Summer M Finlay, Michelle Kennedy, Jessica Bennett, Alana Gall, Juanita Sherwood, Catherine Chamberlain, Michelle Dickson, Nicole Turner, Kristy Williams, Melanie Briggs, Simone Sherriff
pmc-13256005.description: Indigenous women have been nurturing and sustaining our babies through breastfeeding for thousands of years as an important practice for health, wellbeing, community and culture. For many Indigenous women in Western colonized countries breastfeeding and cultural practices have been disrupted by the ongoing impacts of colonization.

pmc-13455837.title: Genetic Ablation and Multi‐Omics Profiling Reveal CEP55 as a Key Driver of Tumorigenesis in Diverse Cancer Models
pmc-13455837.creator: Behnam Rashidieh, Yuanhao Yang, Amanda Louise Bain, Phillip Theron, Catharina Vosloo, Sahar Keshvari, Parinaz Ahangar, Brydie Bowden, Simon M Tria, Ben B Wang, Sandra Isenmann, Nicholas J Westra van Holthe, Zherui Xiong, Hani Vu, Sowmya Sharma, Asmerom Sengal, J Alejandro Lopez, John Finnie, Antonel
pmc-13455837.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). CEP55, a centrosomal protein frequently overexpressed in multiple cancers, is implicated in regulation of genomic instability and PI3K/AKT pathway activation, yet its role in tumor progression and the tumor microenvironment remains incompletely defined. Here, we developed an inducible Cep55 knockout (KO) mouse model and complementary primary, immortalized, and transformed mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) systems and employ integrative multi‐omics analyses to define CEP55‐driven mechanisms and validated findings in human cancer datasets.
